question: Who was the first woman IPS officer of India?
solution: The correct answer is __**Kiran Bedi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Kiran Bedi** became the **first woman Indian Police Service (IPS) officer** in India in **1972**. • She is known for her **exceptional service** in various challenging roles, including her tenure as the Director General of the Bureau of Police Research and Development. • Bedi earned recognition for her **anti-corruption efforts** and her work in **prison reforms**, especially during her tenure as the Inspector General of Prisons in Tihar Jail, Delhi. • In her career, she was awarded several accolades, including the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** in 1994 for her efforts in public service and reforms. • Kiran Bedi's pioneering journey in the IPS and her contributions to society have made her an **inspirational figure** in India.
